answer: A compute exchange rewards fixes to a slow vertex in a workflow graph. Agents commit patch hashes before a hidden benchmark's signal is revealed; independent workers replay each patch as traffic reaches its zenith. The exchange pays once per distinct speedup and splits credit among equivalent patches, regardless of account names. Aliases add no reward: an attacker needs different improvements and must spend compute on each bonded test. This can miss fixes outside the chosen workload, and colluding workers could fake timings, so raw traces and rotating auditors remain necessary.
